newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Escondida mine starts oxides project.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Escondida mine starts oxides project.

text.p: Chile's Minera Escondida Limitada said it will start building work immediately on its $473 million copper oxides project and has received permission to go ahead with the expansion of its sulphides plant.
The mine, the world's largest copper pit, will process oxide ores to produce cathodes using low-cost heap-leaching technology.
"The first production of cathodes is planned for the end of 1998, with the plant expected to reach top capacity in its second year of operation," said the statement.
The plant, which has a design capacity of 125,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year, will have an active life of 14 years.

The mine has also received authorization from the pit's owners and local environment authorities to expand its sulphide concentrator with capacity rising to 175,000 tonnes of mineral a day from its existing level of 105,000 tonnes.
The first phase of the expansion will bring the plant's capacity to 127,000 tonnes a day, said the company.
"(The expansion) is designed to maintain production of concentrates and compensate for the natural fall in ore grades over time," said the statement.
The additional expansion to 175,000 tonnes a day is still under study, it added.
Escondida produced nearly 800,000 tonnes of concentrates last year and 50,000 tonnes of cathodes at its Puerto de Coloso plant. All production was using sulphide ores.
Escondida is owned by RTZ Corp plc and Broken Hill Proprietary.
